tools.name: search_docs
tools.description: Search Appside public developer Markdown; returns source links and excerpts.

tools.name: get_sdk_snippet
tools.description: Get a repository SDK example and its documented verification status. Grant items only on verified backend delivery.

tools.name: get_sdk_status
tools.description: List all SDK download URLs, install instructions and scoped verification status, or select one platform.

tools.name: get_pricing
tools.description: Get Appside published payment fee and fixed-fee policy.

tools.name: register_app
tools.description: List any app or game you built in the Appside public app catalog. No Appside store or account required. tools.name: verify_app
tools.description: Verify a pending registration after publishing the returned token at /.well-known/appside-verify.txt or in a meta name="appside-verify" content="TOKEN" tag on the submitted website. For itch.io, put the token anywhere in the public text of the exact submitted game page (edit its description). Store-

tools.name: get_app
tools.description: Get a verified public app by registration id or slug. Pending, expired or moderated listings are not returned; no private contacts or verification tokens are exposed.

tools.name: search_apps
tools.description: Search verified public apps and games by text, category or playable web build. Pending, expired and moderated listings are excluded.

tools.name: create_account
tools.description: Create an Appside account without a form. Save the bearer token securely; it is shown once. Give the human the claimUrl. Unclaimed accounts expire after 30 days.

tools.name: submit_mcp_server
tools.description: Submit an MCP server for connectivity checks. Domain proof is still required to claim ownership. Pass token or an Authorization: Bearer header on HTTP /mcp. Never publish credentials.

tools.name: claim_mcp_listing
tools.description: Get a domain-proof token with file URLs and DNS TXT records for an MCP listing. Publish the exact token at any supplied URL or TXT name (exact host only). Pass token or an Authorization: Bearer header on HTTP /mcp. Never publish credentials.

tools.name: confirm_mcp_claim
tools.description: Confirm domain proof after publishing the exact verification token at a supplied file URL or DNS TXT name. DNS propagation may take time. Pass token or an Authorization: Bearer header on HTTP /mcp. Never publish credentials.

tools.name: submit_index_entry
tools.description: Submit a web store to the Index for review; does not establish ownership or publish automatically. Pass token or an Authorization: Bearer header on HTTP /mcp. Never publish credentials.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: get_sdk_status, claim_mcp_listing · Private data: register_app, verify_app, get_app, create_account, submit_mcp_server, claim_mcp_listing, confirm_mcp_claim, submit_index_entry · Public sink: register_app, submit_mcp_server, claim_mcp_listing, confirm_mcp_claim, submit_index_entry.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: get_sdk_status, claim_mcp_listing · Private data: register_app, verify_app, get_app, create_account, submit_mcp_server, claim_mcp_listing, confirm_mcp_claim, submit_index_entry · Public sink: register_app, submit_mcp_server, claim_mcp_listing, confirm_mcp_claim, submit_index_entry

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.

findings.title: Tool description changed since last scan
findings.detail: Tool "claim_mcp_listing" changed its description with no version change. Silent description changes are how a trusted server turns malicious after review.

evidence.snippet: before: "Get a domain-proof token and .well-known publication instructions for an MCP listing. Pass token or an Authorization: Bearer header on HTTP /mcp. Never publish credentials." → after: "Get a domain-proof token with file URLs and DNS TXT records for an MCP listing. Publish the exact token at any supplied URL or TXT name (exact host only). Pass token or an Authorization: Bearer header on HTTP /mcp. Never publish credentials."

findings.remediation: Re-review the tool before continuing to trust it.
